title: Crypto declines as inflation persists and banks expand digital-asset plans; portfolio at $65,293
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $74,000, down 0.3% over 24 hours, while ether fell 1.6% to about $2,055. The broader crypto market lost 0.8%, leaving total capitalization around $2.52 trillion. Ether's 11.3% weekly decline was roughly twice bitcoin's 5.6% drop. Selling pressure remains broader than either asset, with inflation and the outlook for interest rates providing an important backdrop.

The new US inflation report showed consumer prices rising 0.4% in October, down from September's 0.6%. Prices excluding food and energy increased 0.3%. Shelter accounted for more than thirty percent of the monthly headline increase, while food rose 0.5%. Inflation has slowed, but these figures still leave limited room for confidence in easier monetary policy. For crypto, that keeps financing conditions relevant to demand for risk assets; the release alone cannot explain every price move.

Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank are among institutions reported to have committed roughly $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture. Bloomberg's report, covered by CoinDesk, says the funding would cover five years of operating costs for Project Faro, a planned US issuer. A dollar token comes first, with other currencies envisaged later. Funding an issuer gives banks a route into a business already served by crypto companies, although the commitment remains attributed to unnamed sources and participating banks had not confirmed it to CoinDesk.

Plume announced that affiliate Kimber Digital Securities obtained FINRA membership and SEC broker-dealer registration. The firm plans to connect wallet users with tokenized US securities, including fund shares and securities entitlements supported by the existing custody system. That could broaden access through wallets while preserving recognized investor claims. Several described services are still under development, and registration does not mean regulators endorse the products or guarantee their returns.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $65,293: $10,768 in the active treasury and $54,525 in the Safe. Its marked value fell $1,317, or 1.98%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC balances remain about 27.76 million tokens, worth $44,841, or 69% of the total. The Safe's additional $6,352 WETH/ARC pool increases that concentration. Beefy positions total about $2,056, down $49, across pools containing ETH, AERO, bitcoin and other assets.

Aave holds about $7,020 of WETH collateral against $3,146 of USDC debt across both wallets. Health factors fell from 2.18 to 2.14 in the treasury and from 1.74 to 1.71 in the Safe as collateral values declined. Fluid remains about $153 net, but its $1,064 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
